body.statement: For every \(\Phi\in\operatorname{3DNF}(X,Z)\), the compiler \(\mathcal C\) runs in polynomial time and emits a valid instance string \(\mathbf i=\mathcal C(\Phi)\) of length \(O(L^2\log^2(L+2))\) satisfying the encoded unit-cost, singleton-terminal, binary two-mode, equality-or-complement, and nonterminal-degree-eight restrictions; no bound is asserted on the number of guarded-edge copies using one switch coordinate. Its occurrence-pair tests force every budget-\(B\) robust cut to spend exactly one vertex per existential occurrence; its consecutive-copy consistency paths make these choices encode one assignment \(x\in\mathbb B^X\); its universal guards make every switch assignment encode one \(z\in\mathbb B^Z\); and selector isolation ensures that a residual \(T\)-to-\(Y\) path exists exactly when a clause chain for \(\neg\Phi(x,z)\) survives, with no inactive-module bypass. For every auxiliary-inclusive budget-feasible robust cut \(K\), \(\rho(K)\) is an occurrence-endpoint cut with \(|\rho(K)|\le |K|\) and no weaker completion-wise separation. Consequently, \(\exists X\,\forall Z\,\Phi(X,Z)\) holds if and only if some \(J\subseteq W\) with \(|J|\le B\) disconnects \(T\) and \(Y\) in every \(H_h-J\), equivalently if and only if \(\mathcal C(\Phi)\in\mathsf{RSJID}\).
body.justification: This isolates all non-routine reduction invariants, including existential proxy choice, universal switching, selector isolation, and rounding away auxiliary interventions.
body.gap: Bachtler et al. supply a related quantified path-separation skeleton, but their selected arc pairs do not establish these unit-cost proxy-copy and auxiliary-rounding invariants.
body.consumer: The standalone audit gives a QBF implementation a precise extraction and regression-testing contract.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(F=\neg\Phi\), let \(N\) be the number of existential-literal occurrences in \(F\), and put \(B=N\).  For every such occurrence \(o\), the compiler creates the two distinct vertices \(p_o^0,p_o^1\).  It creates one pair-test path
\[
 T-p_o^0-p_o^1-Y,
\]
and, for consecutive occurrences \(o,o'\) of the same existential variable, the two consistency paths
\[
 T-p_o^0-p_{o'}^1-Y,
 \qquad
 T-p_o^1-p_{o'}^0-Y.
\]
The formula module has clause boundaries in series.  Within a clause it has parallel literal branches.  The branch for a positive existential occurrence uses \(p_o^1\), the branch for a negative occurrence uses \(p_o^0\), and a universal branch has one edge guarded by the sign of the corresponding coordinate of \(z\).

There are \(K=O(L)\) modules.  Assign them distinct words of length \(q=\lceil\log_2 K\rceil\).  For an original module edge with tag \(\sigma\in\mathbb B^q\), replace that edge by a path of private subdivision vertices having, in order, one edge guarded by each equality \(h_{s_\ell}=\sigma_\ell\).  Append the universal-literal guard when the original edge carries one.  Each guarded edge therefore uses one switch coordinate and one sign, exactly as required by \(\lambda\).  For a fixed selector assignment, a replacement path joins its two original endpoints if and only if its full tag is selected and its optional literal is true.  If the tag is inactive, the surviving pieces of the replacement path meet at most one original endpoint because all subdivision vertices are private.  Consequently inactive modules contribute only dangling components.  Suppressing active replacement paths and deleting dangling pieces leaves exactly the selected module, or no module for an unused selector word.  This proves selector isolation and rules out a path assembled from different modules.

Now let \(K_0\subseteq W\) be robust with \(|K_0|\le N\).  For each occurrence \(o\), choose the completion whose selector word activates its pair test.  Its residual graph contains the corresponding complete pair-test path, so \(K_0\) must meet that path.  The \(N\) pair-test paths have pairwise disjoint nonterminal vertices: occurrence endpoints belong to one occurrence and all selector subdivisions are private.  Hence \(K_0\) has exactly \(N\) vertices, one from every pair test, and no other vertex.

If the chosen vertex for occurrence \(o\) is a private subdivision vertex, restore it and delete either unselected endpoint \(p_o^0\) or \(p_o^1\).  In the completion activating this pair test, deletion of that endpoint still cuts its only active module.  In a completion selecting another module, the restored subdivision lies in an inactive replacement path and cannot join two original vertices, while deleting an occurrence endpoint can only remove paths.  Thus the replacement preserves separation in every completion and does not increase cost.  Iterating over occurrences is exactly the rounding map \(\rho\).  It produces one deleted endpoint in each occurrence pair and no auxiliary deletion.

For the rounded set, let \(x_o\) be the label of the endpoint that is kept.  The first consistency path survives precisely when \((x_o,x_{o'})=(0,1)\), and the second survives precisely when \((x_o,x_{o'})=(1,0)\).  Robust separation of both modules is therefore equivalent to \(x_o=x_{o'}\).  Chaining consecutive copies makes all copies of each existential variable equal and defines one assignment \(x\in\mathbb B^X\).

Fix this \(x\) and a completion value \(z\).  An existential branch in the active formula module survives exactly when its literal is true under \(x\), and a universal branch survives exactly when its guard literal is true under \(z\).  A clause block connects its boundaries exactly when at least one of its literals is true.  Since clause blocks are composed in series and their occurrence vertices are not identified across clauses, the formula module contains a \(T\)-to-\(Y\) path exactly when every clause is true, namely when \(F(x,z)=1\).  Thus a robust rounded cut exists if and only if some \(x\) makes \(F(x,z)=0\) for every \(z\), equivalently if and only if \(\exists x\,\forall z\,\Phi(x,z)=1\).  The converse uses the same calculation: delete \(p_o^{1-x_o}\) for every occurrence.  Pair and consistency modules are cut, and the formula module is cut for every \(z\).

It remains to audit size and restrictions.  Before selector subdivision there are \(O(L)\) vertices and edges.  Subdivision multiplies this by \(O(\log(L+2))\).  The explicit vertex, edge, and guard tables therefore have polynomial size.  A selector coordinate occurs on \(O(L)\) guarded edges, and a universal coordinate occurs on at most \(O(L)\) guarded edges.  The explicitly listed induced equality-or-complement relation consequently has at most \(O(L^2\log(L+2))\) pairs; with \(O(\log(L+2))\) bits per indexed row, the complete canonical string has length \(O(L^2\log^2(L+2))\).

Every cost is one and all observed variables are binary.  Each occurrence endpoint has bidirected degree at most two in its pair test, at most four in the two predecessor/successor consistency relations, and two in its literal branch, totaling eight.  Clause junctions have degree at most six and all private subdivisions have degree two.  Subdivision does not increase the degree of an original endpoint.  The terminals alone may have unbounded degree.  Each switch is binary and every use of a coordinate is an equality or complement guard.  The selector and universal coordinates can have nonconstant guard fanout; this is why no constant guard-list bound is claimed.  All counts and tables are constructible by nested scans over the formula occurrences, so the compiler runs in polynomial time.  Constant formulas and unused existential variables can be decided or discarded in polynomial preprocessing.  This proves the corrected audit.
